audit_kind: Source, evidence and infrastructure hash consistency review; no recompilation
method: Read each of seven existing verification receipts and compute its current SHA-256. The receipt digest is identification, not independent authentication.
Resolve module source paths from the repository when prefixed experiments/, otherwise relative to the receipt directory. Compare current bytes with each recorded module source hash.
Resolve compiler logs relative to the receipt directory and compare recorded log/output digests. Compare checker, compiler and applicable toolchain digests.

For each bound INPUTS.json, verify the manifest hash, every saved source snapshot and every saved inherited input hash. For the core/tree baseline manifest, verify each archived and live ancestor file.

Audit totals are calculated from each receipt module declaration map, not inferred from filenames. Repeated imported declarations across receipts are deliberately counted per receipt, not as independent new theorems.
Use existing reported axiom maps only; this audit does not replay proof checking, re-evaluate compiler trust or establish theoretical completeness.
scope_limits: These are current-byte consistency checks against already saved evidence. They do not constitute fresh Lean validation.
Separate public entry points and separate checkers are legitimate modular organization; successful shared imports do not establish physical history composition.
A supplied local law is not thereby external to generative reality. Missing formal relations, unexplained theory connections and substantive counterevidence remain distinct under NONDUAL-METHOD.md.

default_core.policy: Exact historical declarations may retain their recorded dependencies; every new/deeper theorem audit must be empty. This audit does not widen that policy.

core_tree.policy: Each inherited module retains its exact recorded declaration dependency map; all eleven new theorem audits must be empty.

connected_family.policy: The connected, applicability, nondual applicability and pretraining checkers disclose standard dependencies (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice), reject custom axioms/placeholders, and enforce named empty-dependency contracts. They do not assert the entire closure is empty-dependency.

coformation.policy: The additive coformation checker accepts only disclosed standard named dependencies; it does not enforce the default-core empty-new-dependency policy.
